Verified:
- durable skeleton commit/PR existed before the remote probe;
- already-authorized SSH transport and ordinary remote shell execution work;
- echo, ls, and uname controls returned 0;
- captured host snapshot (87% memory free, zero swap/compressor/pageouts, unlimited RSS/data, root 18% used) materially weakens system-wide OOM as the explanation for this window;
- no matching DiagnosticReport or bounded unified-log kill record was found;
- the exact Codex dispatch/helper failure was not reproduced, so neither victim nor killer is identified;
- the report appropriately does not infer cause from status 137.

Review corrections / avoidable friction:
- `/bin/true` is an invalid control path on this Darwin installation; exit 127 is path error, not evidence of runtime incompatibility. A future probe should use `/usr/bin/true` and/or shell builtin `true`.
- PR #171 contains eight unrelated Persistent Commander/reporter files inherited from an unmerged predecessor branch. The forensic evidence is reviewable, but this PR is not merge-ready as a clean forensic unit.

Last verified-good transition:
Wolfram -> authorized SSH alias -> Darwin shell -> ordinary leaf commands.

First missing transition:
an observable invocation through the exact failing Darwin Codex execution handoff with PID/PPID and wait-status correlation.

Minimum next safe continuation:
instrument or wrap one already-supported failing Codex command at the existing dispatch boundary to record timestamp, process tree, and raw wait status, then correlate only that window with DiagnosticReports/unified log. Do not reinstall/update first. Continue from the exact forensic artifact; do not rerun #160/GD2.

Wise Broker:
The result does not explain #160. It does prove a valuable negative: Darwin itself, SSH transport, and the ordinary shell were available during the probe, so a machine-wide outage is unsupported. #160 linkage remains UNKNOWN.

No model identity, effort, token usage, or account-level run attribution was exposed; none is claimed.
